result.question: Find surface fields/applications where four deep structural results reappear (method transfer, not analogy). Strata: (1) local coherence vs global realizability on cyclic overlap structures — window marginals on rings of contexts, coherence polytope C vs realizability polytope R, a per-length decidable "winding criterion" for shift-invariant protocols; (2) two tokens moving in lockstep on a primitive digraph never occupying the same vertex (off-diagonal pair graph bar-D), question: is every strongly connected component containing a swap (a,b)->(b,a) aperiodic / does it contain a cocyclic pair ("reach lemma"); (3) finitely coherent states with no sigma-additive realization witnessed by no finite sub-object (sigma-essential states on concrete sigma-orthoposets / Dynkin systems); (4) conservativity of an idealized completion (global joint, sigma-additive extension, process) over local data — when the scaffold proves nothing new about the windows. For each stratum, find areas beyond quantum foundations, graphical models/loopy BP, relational database acyclicity, frustration/Z2 synchronization, Abramsky sheaf contextuality, symbolic dynamics weak mixing, Higman orbital graphs, Cerny synchronizing automata, MAPF/token swapping, de Finetti finite additivity (already known). Prioritize: candidate existing theorems that could prove the open reach lemma (funnel case); fields where the winding criterion would be a new result; crowdedness assessment per site. Output a ranked map with citations.
result.summary: The search found no existing theorem that proves the open reach lemma (funnel case). For stratum 2 the nearest results are the no-meet matroid of Ben-Ameur et al. and Kari's stable-pair form of road colouring. Both work with the same object, two lockstep walks avoiding the diagonal, but neither addresses aperiodicity of swap-containing SCCs or cocyclic pairs. Stratum 1 is the most crowded. Vorob'ev 1962 and junction-tree theory settle C = R on acyclic structures. Pivato 2001 poses the shift-invariant Z^D extension problem directly, and his periodic extensions on Z/P are ring realizations. On the infinite line the 1D shift-invariant problem is trivial. A gap between coherence and realizability appears only on finite rings, the periodic quotient, so any novelty for the per-length winding criterion is confined to that cyclic, shift-invariant periodic regime. In 2D the problem is open-ended or undecidable for general alphabets (Wang–Navascués). Stratum 4 conservativity has two real method-transfer homes: (a) Sherali–Adams/Lasserre exactness at treewidth-based levels, and (b) invariance of k-local LPs under C^k (k-WL) equivalence (Atserias–Maneva, Grohe–Otto). Stratum 3 surfaced nothing new outside the already-known finite-additivity line. Schervish–Seidenfeld–Kadane conglomerability is the Boolean prototype of 'no finite sub-object witnesses'; it is a rhyme with stratum 3, not a transfer.

findings.claim: RANK 1 (stratum 1, highest crowding risk): Pivato's 'Building a stationary stochastic process from a finite-dimensional marginal' (Canad. J. Math. 53(2), 2001, 382-413) poses the general problem of extending a shift-invariant window marginal mu_U on A^U, U finite in Z^D, to a stationary field on Z^D. Its periodic-extension variant, measures on (Z/P1)+...+(Z/PD) with periodic boundary, is exactly realization on a cyclic ring when D=1. The paper calls D=1 classical and surveys it. For D>1 it gives only some necessary and some sufficient conditions. It also asks when the extension can be ergodic, (quasi)periodic or weakly mixing, and links the problem to invariant measures of SFTs and cellular automata (MSC 37B10). This is the first paper to check against the winding criterion: does its §8, or the classical D=1 work it surveys, already contain a per-period test for periodic extendability?
findings.evidence: Claims 0, 17, 18, 19 (all primary; votes 3-0, 2-1, 3-0, 3-0). Verifiers confirmed the quoted abstract text and §8 '(quasi)Periodic, Ergodic, and Mixing Extensions' with the M=(Z/P1)+...+(Z/PD) setup.

findings.claim: Stratum 1 scoping: on the infinite line, every locally coherent shift-invariant marginal extends (C = R), through a Markov-chain construction. A gap between C and R therefore appears only on finite rings, the periodic quotient. Standard example: P(01)=P(10)=1/2 extends on Z but cannot be realized on any odd ring. So the winding criterion's content is specifically a per-length periodicity obstruction, and that is where any novelty claim must sit.
findings.evidence: Claim 3 (3-0). The PIRSA 2017 talk abstract says verbatim 'triviality of the marginal problem for 1D TI distributions'. The verifier supplied the odd-ring counterexample. Pivato also calls D=1 classical.

findings.claim: Stratum 1, dimension boundary: for 2D translation-invariant distributions, Wang–Navascués solve the membership problem exactly for small alphabets (d=2,3 nearest-neighbour; d=2 nearest plus next-nearest), and the realizable sets are polytopes. For general local dimension, exact energy-per-site computation is undecidable, and for d≥2947 the nearest-neighbour marginal set is not even semi-algebraic. Any analogue of the winding criterion on finite L×L tori is a finite LP and decidable. The barrier lies only on the infinite Z^2 lattice. Their paper treats realizable sets only and has no coherence polytope C, so the parallel is with R alone.
findings.evidence: Claims 1, 2 (3-0, primary, Proc. R. Soc. A 474:20170822, 2018). Verifiers flagged that 'no decidable winding-type criterion in 2D' is an inference about the infinite lattice, not about tori.

findings.claim: Stratum 1 baseline (known, crowded): Vorob'ev 1962 proves that every pairwise-consistent family on a finite complex extends iff the complex is 'regular'. Regularity is an ear-elimination condition, identified with GYO/alpha-acyclicity by Beeri–Fagin–Maier–Yannakakis 1983. The junction-tree theorem gives the same C = R on hypertrees. Rings of L≥3 windows are non-regular. The ring with stride-1 windows has no proper vertices; general rings get stuck at an edge-cycle. Vorob'ev gives only a qualitative dichotomy, with no per-length or quantitative description of C\R on cyclic complexes. That leaves room for the winding criterion relative to this line, subject to the Pivato check.
findings.evidence: Claims 4, 5, 11 (all 3-0, primary). Verifier correction: the claim that no maximal face of a ring has a proper vertex holds for stride-1 windows only; the conclusion (non-regular) holds generally.

findings.claim: Stratum 4 (method transfer, Sherali–Adams/Lasserre): the level-(t+1) Sherali–Adams and level-(t+v) Lasserre relaxations equal the integer hull, with t the treewidth of the canonical hypergraph, and the bounds are sharp in the worst case. This gives an explicit level at which lifted local-consistency data becomes conservative over global realizability. A ring of contexts has bounded treewidth, so R on a finite ring is a fixed-level SA polytope. The winding criterion can then be read as describing the gap between level-1 (local) consistency and that exact level under shift symmetry. The condition is sufficient, not necessary: low treewidth is not necessary for tightness (Rowland–Pacchiano–Weller 2017).
findings.evidence: Claim 12 (3-0), but the source is an unrefereed 2004 UC Berkeley tech report. The ring/treewidth reading is synthesis, not sourced.

findings.claim: Stratum 4 (method transfer, finite model theory): any k-local LP has the same feasibility on C^k-equivalent structures, and level-ck SDPs on C^{ck}-equivalent ones. The proof pushes a feasible solution through a Sherali–Adams fractional isomorphism. SA level k sits between C^k and C^{k-1} (Atserias–Maneva 2013; Malkin), strictly for k≥3 (Grohe–Otto 2015), and a combined LP ISO(k-1/2) characterizes C^k exactly. This is a formal theorem of the form 'the scaffold proves nothing new beyond k-local data', which is the shape of stratum 4. It transfers only if the scaffold LP is k-local in the atomic-type sense.
findings.evidence: Claim 13 (3-0) was verified against Grohe–Otto primary. Claim 14 (2-1) rests on the author's talk slides. Index shifts between SA level and C^k are loose.

findings.claim: RANK 1 for stratum 2 (closest existing object, not a proof route): Ben-Ameur, Kushik, Maddaloni, Neto and Watel define the no-meet matroid (DAM 354, 2024). Its independent sets are the sets of start vertices whose synchronous infinite walks can avoid ever sharing a vertex, and independence is testable in polynomial time. The class sits strictly between transversal matroids and gammoids. Its rank equals the largest order of a collection of vertex-disjoint cycles (Ben-Ameur–Maddaloni, Networks 84(2), 2024, which also gives a cops-and-robber meeting-time game). For two tokens, independence of {a,b} is exactly whether the off-diagonal pair graph bar-D has an infinite forward walk from (a,b). The papers neither say whether swaps count as meetings nor address SCC periodicity or cocyclic pairs, so they do not reach the funnel case. The authors' meeting-time and cops-and-robber techniques are the nearest active toolbox.
findings.evidence: Claims 7 (2-1), 8 (3-0), 9 (3-0). The cycle characterization appears only in the Networks abstract. Swap semantics are unverified pending the full text (DOI 10.1016/j.dam.2022.12.008).

findings.claim: Stratum 2 (known area, possible technique): Culik–Karhumäki–Kari showed road colouring is equivalent to every strongly connected aperiodic graph having a colouring with at least one stable pair. Trahtman's 2009 proof works through this reduction. The reduction from a global question to the existence of one pair in the pair automaton has the same shape as the reach lemma. A stable pair is a diagonal-reaching property, though, whereas the reach lemma is about diagonal-avoiding SCC structure. This is a candidate technique to check, not a theorem that applies. Vocabulary warning: 'primitive automaton' in Rystsov–Szykuła means a transition monoid with no nontrivial congruence, not digraph primitivity, so hypotheses do not transfer from that line.
findings.evidence: Claims 6 and 10 (3-0). The Kari abstract says only 'our earlier papers'; the attribution to Culik–Karhumäki–Kari comes from IJFCS 2002, which was not re-fetched. A related claim that treats road colouring as the same problem as the reach lemma was refuted 1-2.

findings.claim: Stratum 3 (known, rhyme not transfer): Schervish–Seidenfeld–Kadane 1984 show that for a finitely additive probability P on a σ-field, the extent of non-conglomerability of every coherent extension equals the weight of the purely finitely additive Yosida–Hewitt part. So σ-additivity is equivalent to conglomerability on every countable partition. On finite partitions the law of total probability always holds, so no finite sub-partition detects the failure. This is the Boolean prototype of 'witnessed by no finite sub-object'. It sits in the de Finetti finite-additivity line already listed as known, and the search found no non-Boolean or orthoposet analogue.
findings.evidence: Claim 15 (3-0) and claim 16 (2-1). The source is a secondary survey (Berti–Miranda–Rigo) faithfully reporting SSK 1984 (Z. Wahrsch. 66). Verifier correction: countably additive P can still fail conglomerability on uncountable partitions, so the accurate wording is 'infinite partitions'.

result.caveats:
The verifiers disagree about Pivato. The verifiers of claims 0 and 17 read the abstract as saying the D>1 problem is 'not formally decidable', but a separate claim stating exactly that was refuted 1-2. Read the full text before citing undecidability from Pivato; Wang–Navascués is the safer citation for 2D undecidability.

Two refuted leads should not be used. A winding-number argument for collisions on cycles (arXiv:2506.21929) was refuted 0-3. A claim that De Simone–Pták extends measures on 'circle' coarse-grained spaces was refuted 1-2, although that paper is worth checking against the shelf for stratum 1/3 crowding.

All 'method transfer' readings are synthesis, not source statements. These include the ring treewidth reading for Sherali–Adams, k-local LP invariance as stratum-4 conservativity, and the no-meet matroid as stratum 2.

No field for stratum 3 beyond the known finite-additivity line was found, and no candidate proof of the reach lemma (funnel case) was found. Coverage for strata 2 and 3 is thin, and absence here does not mean absence in the literature.

Per CLAUDE.md, grep notes/literature_review (the *_byhand_read.md and *_SOURCE_CHECK_* files) for Pivato, Vorob'ev, Wang–Navascués, Ben-Ameur and Schervish before treating any of these as new leads. Several sources are talk slides, abstracts or tech reports rather than full refereed texts.
openQuestions: Does the classical D=1 literature Pivato surveys (§8 periodic extensions on Z/P) already contain a per-period criterion for when a shift-invariant window marginal is realizable on the ring Z/L? If it does, the winding criterion is prior art rather than a new result.

Do Ben-Ameur et al. count two walks swapping along an edge as a meeting, and do their meeting-time or cops-and-robber arguments give any control over the period of SCCs in the off-diagonal pair graph (the funnel case)?
Can the stable-pair reduction behind Trahtman's road colouring proof be dualised to a diagonal-avoiding statement, namely the existence of a cocyclic pair in a swap-containing SCC?
Is there a non-Boolean (orthoposet or Dynkin-system) analogue of the Schervish–Seidenfeld–Kadane conglomerability equality, and would it give an instrument for detecting σ-essential states?

refuted.claim: For D > 1 the paper says the general extendibility problem is not formally decidable. This makes the decidability of a per-length winding criterion depend on dimension: undecidability is claimed in higher dimension, which contrasts with a decidable criterion for one-dimensional (cyclic or shift-invariant) protocols.

For larger alphabets in 2D, the TI nearest-neighbor marginal set is neither a polytope nor semi-algebraic, and computing the exact ground-state energy per site of arbitrary 2D TI Hamiltonians is undecidable. This marks where a decidable per-length winding-type criterion cannot extend: from 1D/cyclic overlap structures to 2D lattices.

In Kari's setting (a strongly connected, aperiodic digraph with uniform out-degree k, colored so each vertex has one outgoing edge of each color), the road coloring conjecture asks for a synchronizing coloring. This is the pair-collapse problem on the pair graph, which is close to the reach-lemma setting of stratum 2 (tokens on a primitive digraph).

On a cycle, collision is forced quickly with high probability, so no evasive walks exist on cycles. The proof uses a winding-number invariant of the two walks, which is a cyclic winding obstruction with the same flavour as the winding criterion in stratum 1 and the winding-2 scope of stratum 2.

De Simone and Pták (Bull. Polish Acad. Sci. Math. 2006, pp. 1-11) show that a measure on a finite coarse-grained space, and on a 'circle' coarse-grained space, always extends to the whole power algebra. This is a known local-to-global extension result on a cyclic overlap structure, so it bears on the crowdedness of stratum 1 (ring of contexts) more than on stratum 3.
